analysis:
Integration of all four units: the PR adds require_supported_macos() to scripts/install.sh (head ~447-464), called at ~592 right after select_provider_identity. It refuses a new install on macOS major <27 before download and permits reinstall or repair when $BIN_DIR/$CLI_NAME or $PROVIDER_CONFIG exists. Unknown or non-numeric versions return 0. The other files are docs and a changelog (consistent with TB-011's note that new macOS27+ onboarding waits for App Attest) plus the SupportedMacOSTests unit tests in scripts/test-install-onboarding.py.

Security assessment: the gate only narrows installs. It is client-side onboarding UX, not an authorization boundary. Serving authorization remains coordinator-side (A-016, TB-011, T-052, TB-002), and the operator controls their own machine (ADV-001), so bypassing the gate by pre-creating a file or editing the script grants nothing. It runs before any download, so bundle-hash, codesign and staged-verification controls (T-013, T-034) are unchanged. MACOS is only used in a numeric comparison after a digit-only case guard, and is otherwise echoed, so there is no injection. Fail-open on unknown versions is consistent with configure_device_verification and only permits an install that existing controls still gate. No change to App Attest proof lifetimes, qualification, key custody or encryption.

Remaining uncertainty (not a finding): the variable definitions (MACOS, BIN_DIR, PROVIDER_CONFIG, PROVIDER_LABEL) lie outside the supplied patch excerpts. The platform-served install.sh copy must be re-synced (outside the supplied evidence). The changed docs make no claim that alters the security posture.
